ambiguity: Three serde conventions sit side by side in PocketConfig: plain f64 with no default (stepover, depth, line 494), Option<f64> with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)] (ramp_feed_rate, line 504), and a named default fn (region_ordering, line 517). The old-file load behaviour differs for each. The CLAUDE.md files do not say which one a new numeric field must use.

Two closest examples: finishing_passes (usize, special GUI row, read by cutting_levels at catalog.rs:1405 and by DepthStepping) and stepover (f64, dv_pill row, macro accessor, feeds readers). A depth-like field copies the first. A cut-geometry field copies the second.

Option<f64> with None meaning a derived value (ramp_feed_rate) or a plain f64 with a fixed default (angle, stepover). The ramp_feed_rate pattern also pulls in feeds provenance (feeds/provenance.rs, params.rs:455), which a plain dial must not copy.

Validation has four homes: #[param(range)] (schema, GUI clamp, MCP refuse), a viz OP_UI_ROWS validate arm (GUI only), core compute/validate.rs stale-default checks, and a kernel guard (ops/drill.rs fed_descents). Each has a precedent. The docs do not say which one owns which rule. The operator ruling 2026-10-15 (single-field floor goes in the schema, not in the GUI) covers only one case.

Contour pattern and Zigzag pattern of Pocket are two LayeredOp adapters in one file (PocketContour at clearing_2d.rs:176 and ZigzagRaster at :247, shared with the Zigzag op). The new value may belong to one pattern, to both, or to ZigzagConfig as well. The GUI already hides angle unless the pattern is Zigzag (boundary_2d.rs:108).
